analysis_steps.goal: Image continuum and lines, self-calibrate two fields

method.value: CASA clean with Briggs robust 0, multiscale, 3 sigma threshold; self-cal on SMM11 and SMM4

evidence.quote: The visibilities were Fourier transformed and CLEANed with a Briggs robust parameter of 0.0 and a threshold of 3$\sigma$ for all the lines and continuum data.

validation.value: Self-cal kept only where rms improved significantly

evidence.quote: We did not adopt the self-calibrated results for the other three fields because the rms noise level was not improved significantly in those fields.

analysis_steps.goal: Measure continuum and C18O source properties

method.value: 2D Gaussian fits for positions and deconvolved sizes; peak and total flux within 3 sigma contours after primary beam correction; uncertainty sigma_i*sqrt(4*Omega)

evidence.quote: the uncertainty of each flux density was calculated from the rms noise level of intensity $\sigma _i$ in the unit of Jy beam$^{-1}$ and the integrated area $\Omega$ in the unit of beam as $\sigma_i\sqrt{4\Omega}$
the fitting was simultaneously done using a double-component 2D Gaussian function

method.value: Intensity-weighted PA, length, opening angle from CLEAN-deconvolved 12CO moment 0 maps (5 sigma cutoff); intensity-weighted velocity; tau_dyn = r/v

evidence.quote: the $^{12}$CO moment 0 maps were deconvolved in the way of CLEAN: finding peaks in a moment 0 map, recording the peaks as “CLEAN components", subtracting beam (Gaussian) functions from the moment 0 map, and then repeating these down to a $5\sigma$ cutoff.

assumptions.value: Systemic velocities from C18O Gaussian fits; S68Nb1 assumed same as S68Nc1

evidence.quote: The systemic velocity of S68Nb1 was assumed to be the same as that of S68Nc1 since the C$^{18}$O line is not detected in S68Nb1.

method.value: Wind-driven-shell model fit to binarized moment 0 maps and PV diagrams (5 sigma)

evidence.quote: the $^{12}$CO moment 0 maps and $^{12}$CO position-velocity (PV) diagrams are fitted with the wind-driven-shell model (cite: shu91; lee00)

key_parameters.value: Low-velocity ranges filled with emission, e.g. 6-10 km/s in S68N

fitting.value: MCMC with emcee; log likelihood -chi^2/2; uncertainties from 5th and 95th percentiles

evidence.quote: The log likelihood is $-\chi ^{2} /2$, where $\chi^2$ is the sum of squared differences between the model and the observations (i.e., unity or zero).

validation.value: SMM4B excluded since single shell inappropriate

evidence.quote: Our single shell model is not appropriate to fit such a complex velocity structure.

method.value: Continuum peak to H2 column and central density (Gaussian line-of-sight profile), then Jeans length

evidence.quote: the H$_2$ column density is converted to the central number density $n_{\rm H_2}$ by assuming a Gaussian density profile along the line of sight

assumptions.value: kappa(850um)=0.035 cm2/g, beta=1, T=10 K, mu=2.37

evidence.quote: We adopt a dust opacity coefficient of $\kappa (850\ \ensuremath{\mu}m) = 0.035\ {\rm cm}^2\,{\rm g}^{-1}$ (cite: an.wi05), an opacity index, $\beta=1$, and a temperature of 10 K

validation.value: Sensitivity to beta, temperature, flux error tested

evidence.quote: If the temperature is relatively high as prestellar sources, $\sim 15$ K, the density is two times lower, and the ratio is $\sim 40\%$ lower.

method.value: From continuum and C18O integrated intensity at continuum peak, optically thin, LTE

evidence.quote: The temperature is assumed to be 20 K for the protostellar sources (Group 1 and 3) (cite: leek14) and 10 K for the prestellar sources (Group 2)
